Law Passed: Alaska HB 25 (Disposable Food Service Ware), which would have banned single-use polystyrene foam foodware containers, cups, plates, and lids in restaurants and state agencies, was vetoed by Governor Mike Dunleavy on June 24-25, 2026. No EPR packaging producer responsibility law exists or is pending in Alaska.
Status Detail: HB 25 passed the Alaska House and Senate in spring 2026 with bipartisan support but was vetoed by Governor Dunleavy on June 24-25, 2026, citing concerns about implementation timelines and costs to rural businesses. The bill was a material ban/restriction on polystyrene foodservice packaging, not a full EPR producer responsibility program. No Alaska packaging EPR bill covering poly bags, plastic film, paper bagging, mesh bagging, or other packaging categories has been introduced or is pending as of October 2026.

Law Passed: Hawaii enacted Act 103 (HB 750) on May 27, 2025 — a pre-EPR needs assessment law covering all packaging materials and paper products (including bags and film). A full EPR program bill (HB 1264) was carried into the 2026 session but died on May 8, 2026 without passing. No full EPR packaging law has been enacted. The Act 103 advisory council held its first meeting on August 27, 2026, and the needs assessment report is due to the legislature by December 31, 2027.
Status Detail: Act 103 (HB 750, signed May 27, 2025) requires the Hawaii Department of Health to conduct a statewide needs assessment for an EPR program covering all packaging materials and paper products, funded at $1.5 million per year for FY2026 and FY2027. The advisory council — which includes representatives from waste, recycling, compost, reuse/refill, and producer trade associations — held its inaugural meeting on August 27, 2026, and the needs assessment document is being developed through 2026–2027 with a final report due to the legislature by December 31, 2027. A separate full EPR program bill (HB 1264, covering primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging including bags) was carried over into the 2026 session but was marked dead as of May 8, 2026 when the legislature adjourned sine die.

Law Passed: Maine LD 1541 (2021), amended by LD 1423 (signed June 20, 2025) — the Stewardship Program for Packaging — is enacted law. Implementation is stalled: the DEP's first RFP for a Stewardship Organization (SO) closed August 18, 2026 with zero proposals, including a declination by Circular Action Alliance. On September 11, 2026, DEP announced it is revising the RFP; no reissue date has been set and no SO is under contract. All producer registration, reporting, and fee obligations are suspended until an SO is contracted.
Status Detail: DEP published an SO RFP on June 15, 2026; it drew no submissions by the August 18 deadline, and CAA — the PRO administering six other state EPR programs — formally declined to bid. On September 11, 2026 DEP confirmed it is revising the RFP and will notify stakeholders when the revised document is available, pushing every downstream compliance date — producer registration, startup invoicing, and municipal reimbursements — to indeterminate future dates. The failed procurement has also raised the possibility of further legislative amendments to Maine's underlying EPR statute.

Law Passed: Maryland SB 901 (Packaging and Paper Products – Producer Responsibility Plans Act) was signed into law on May 13, 2025. Implementing regulations under COMAR 26.04.14 became effective May 25, 2026. The program is now in active implementation, with MDE Advisory Council meetings scheduled through December 2026 and additional rulemaking ongoing.
Status Detail: SB 901 covers all consumer packaging and paper products broadly — including primary, secondary, and tertiary/shipping packaging made of any material (plastic, paper, metal, glass, etc.) — with limited exemptions for infant formula, medical/hazardous materials, and de minimis producers (under 1 ton or under $2M global revenue). The Circular Action Alliance (CAA) is the sole designated PRO; producers were required to submit an initial Simplified Supply Report by May 31, 2026 and register with MDE by July 1, 2026. The first Producer Responsibility Plan is due July 1, 2028, with producer cost-share obligations ramping to 50% by July 2028, 75% by July 2029, and 90% by July 2030. MDE has described the May 2026 regulations as a first phase, with further rulemakings anticipated on fee structures, ecomodulation, and covered-material definitions.

Law Passed: Missouri HB 3504 (Producer Responsibility Program for Statewide Recycling Act) introduced February 26, 2026; referred to House Emerging Issues Committee on May 15, 2026; did not advance further before the 2026 regular session adjourned sine die.
Status Detail: HB 3504 would require producers of packaging and paper products — including all packaging types — to join or form a nonprofit producer responsibility organization (PRO) to fund and manage a statewide recycling system, with penalties of $5,000 per day per violation for noncompliance. The bill was introduced by a single Democratic sponsor, referred to the House Emerging Issues Committee on May 15, 2026, and did not advance; analysts characterized Missouri as a political longshot for near-term enactment. The 2026 Missouri regular session has adjourned sine die, meaning the bill expired without passage and would need to be reintroduced in the 2027 session.
